chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ṭayyib, from ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn Manṣūr, from Muḥammad ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, who said:

I heard Yaḥyā ibn Aktham, the judge of Sāmarrāʾ, after I had exerted myself with him, debated him, conversed with him, kept company with him, and asked him about the knowledge of the family of Muḥammad. So he said: One day, as I entered circling the grave of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, I saw Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Riḍā عليه السلام circling it.

So I debated with him regarding questions I had, and he brought them forth to me. Then I said to him: By Allah, I wish to ask you a question, and by Allah, I am ashamed of that. He said to me: I shall inform you before you ask me; you want to ask me about the Imam. I said: By Allah, that is indeed it. He said: I am he. I said: A sign? Then there was a staff in his hand, and it spoke and said: Indeed, my master is the Imam of this time, and he is the Proof.

key_terms.إِمَامُ هَذَا الزَّمَانِ: the rightful Imam of the present age
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the divinely designated leader whose authority is being asked about
key_terms.الْحُجَّةُ: the divine proof and authoritative representative of Allah over creation
key_terms.عَصًا: a staff that serves as the medium of a miracle
key_terms.عَلَامَةً: a sign or proof requested to verify the claim
key_terms.عُلُومِ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: the divinely granted knowledge of the family of Muḥammad

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe a sign proving the Imamate of Imām Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Riḍā عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an encounter in which Yaḥyā ibn Aktham is confronted with the extraordinary knowledge and sign of Imamate of Imām Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Riḍā عليه السلام. The report emphasizes recognition of the true Imam through divinely granted knowledge and a manifest miracle, affirming his status as the ḥujjah over the people.
